newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Celuloza bourse price seen up at PLN 20.
newsitem.headline: Polish Celuloza bourse price seen up at PLN 20.

text.p: Analysts expect the shares of Poland's largest paper firm, Celuloza Swiecie SA, to sell at about 20 zlotys at a special Warsaw bourse session on Tuesday, above the minimum price of 15 zlotys.

The treasury ministry has offered 15 percent or 7.5 million shares of Celuloza in a public subscription at a minimum price of 15 zlotys. The final strike price will be determined and shares allotted at the special session today. Results are due at about 1230 gmt after the market's close.
The bourse debut is slated for April 25.

Analysts interviewed by Reuters said paper firms from emerging markets were trading at 10 times earnings on average, but Swiecie should trade at a premium because of its smaller exposure to cyclical pressures, planned cost-cutting measures and the expected increase in earnings in 1998.

"The price should be set at a premium to, let's say, Czech (paper) firms...a fair price would be 19-20 zlotys, but the quick procedure (of allotting the shares) might make it slightly higher," said Grzegorz Cimochowski of ING Barings brokerage.
He added that the price of 20 zlotys would make the company trade at 13-14 times 1997 earnings. "A P/E ratio of 13 or 14 is what a reasonable investor should accept," he said.
Analysts also said the firm's large capitalisation of $250 million at the minimum price of 15 zlotys and over $300 million at 20 zlotys, made it attractive for foreign investors.
The state treasury offered 7.5 million Swiecie shares or 15 percent of the company in a public subscription last week.
Analysts also said the offer was even more attractive thanks to the quick procedure of allotting shares only few days after the subscription period.
IB Austria said in an April 8 report that the minimum offer price was at a 40-70 percent discount to leading international paper companies and Warsaw bourse's top industrials.

Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage said the fair current value of Celuloza was 15-16 zlotys, but investors would price taking into account an expected improvement of climate for paper firms and future Celuloza profits.
Pospieszynski saw both the strike and debut price at between 20 and 25 zlotys.

"The average P/E for papper firms on emerging markets was 10 at the end of 1996 and the P/BV below one, so Swiecie should cost 15-16 zlotys, but investors will be pricing in the firm's prospects after possible cost cuts and climate improvement," he said.
At 15 zlotys Celuloza had a 1996 P/E of 10 and a price-to-book value above one.

Some analysts said that the debut price on Friday should not differ much from Tuesday's strike price as there were only a few days between allotting the shares and the bourse debut, but others still saw some upside potential.

"This kind of share sale eliminates the possibility of irrational valuation...so one shouldn't expect a 50-percent jump on debut, but those, who bid too low may want to buy the shares on the exchange at higher price," Cimochowski said.
